title: Site area merit assessment criteria
text: M4.1.1 Development of the type and density indicated by the density code designated in the scheme. M4.1.2 The WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a green title lot or survey-strata lot (excluding battleaxe lots) with a minimum and/or average site area up to 5 per cent less than that specified in Table 3B where it will: i. not create more than one lot with a reduced minimum lots size; ii. facilitate the protection of an environmental or heritage feature; iii. facilitate the retention of a significant element that contributes toward an existing streetscape worthy of retention; iv. facilitate the development of lots with separate and sufficient frontage to more than one public street; v. overcome a special or unusual limitation on the development of the land imposed by its size, shape or other feature; vi. allow land to be developed with housing of the same type and form as land in the vicinity and which would not otherwise be able to be developed; or vii. achieve specific objectives of the local planning framework. M4.1.3 In addition to M4.1.2, the WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a green title lot, survey-strata lot or strata lot with an average lot size variation greater than five percent than that specified in Table 3B for R10 to R35 lots (base code applied for dual coded land), provided that: i. the site is a corner lot with frontage to two different streets or any other lot with frontage to more than one dedicated street (excluding a primary (red), other regional (blue) or any other major road, including state and federal highways, with access restrictions); ii. all proposed lots comply with the minimum lot size and frontage provisions specified in Table 3B; iii. the width and frontage of the new lots will enable dwellings to have their primary frontage to the different streets; iv. crossovers and driveways to proposed lots are provided in accordance with Australian Standard (AS) 2890 and C3.7 Access; and v. any corner truncation, pedestrian access way, vehicle right of way or laneway widening is excluded from the calculation of the minimum lot size. M4.1.4 The WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a survey-strata lot or strata lot for an existing authorised grouped dwelling development of a lesser minimum and average site area than that specified in Table 3B, where, in the opinion of the WAPC or the local government, the development on the resulting survey-strata or strata lots is consistent with the objectives of the relevant design elements of the R-Codes, and the orderly and proper planning of the locality. M4.1.5 Potential change: New provision to allow for greater subdivision potential on corner lots coded R10-R17.5. Refer to Information Sheet 5: Lot size and density. M4.1.6 Potential change: New provision to allow minimum site area to be reduced up to 10 per cent where the existing dwelling is retained. Refer to Information Sheet 5: Lot size and density.

notes: Merit criteria of element 4.1 (pages 51-53). M4.1.2-M4.1.6 are WAPC/merit matters, also recorded one per file under rules/4.1 as judgment rules in column M (register ch3-091, ch3-092, ch3-094, ch3-097, ch3-098). M4.1.5 and M4.1.6 are flagged potential changes with no operative text. Numbering differs from Chapter 2: M4.1.4 here is strata lots for existing grouped development.
